newsitem.title: TANZANIA: World Bank warns Tanzania on bank restructuring.
newsitem.headline: World Bank warns Tanzania on bank restructuring.

text.p: The World Bank warned Tanzania on Tuesday it would only pay the first installment of a key credit if the government restructured the National Bank of Commerce (NBC).
Tanzania said on Tuesday it would delay restructuring the NBC, its largest commercial bank, until September to consider how to do it.

The Bank's board approved a $125 million structural adjustment credit (SAC) last Friday but would only pay when Tanzania made good promises to restructure the NBC, said World Bank Tanzania Representative Ron Brigish.
The first tranche of SAC is $50 million for balance of payments support with the release date at the Bank's discretion. In total $25 million is earmarked for the NBC's restructuring.
Brigish said he understood a government request for time to build a political consensus on restructuring, but said the issue was seven years old.

"We are basically saying the timetable is not the issue. The issue is action. We will release funds when privatisation and restructuring action are undertaken," Brigish told Reuters. "We think restructuring should take place as soon as possible. There is an issue of confidence in the banking sector."

The World Bank wants Tanzania to split the NBC's assets and distribute them to holding companies or new institutions. Under this scheme NBC would be broken into three smaller banks focusing on trade, regional and micro-finance respectively.
But Tanzania has postponed bank restructuring from July 1 until September to allow time to look at other strategies, said Mkapa's spokesman Patrick Chokala.
"It will allow more time for the government to look at other strategies. Up to now there's only been one -- to split the bank into three," he said.
The break up of NBC, which was founded in 1967, is proving difficult for Tanzanian President Benjamin Mkapa with vocal opposition from bank supporters.
Former president Julius Nyerere, influential despite resigning in 1985, is concerned restructuring the bank would hurt the rural community limiting its access to development credit, diplomats said.
NBC must also decide the fate of an estimated 2,000 employees earmarked for retrenchment from the 4,000 workforce.

The International Monetary Fund approved last November $220 million over three years as part of an enhanced structural adjustment facility for Tanzania. Restructuring NBC and the sale of parastatals was key to the resumption of credit.
